prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single universally “best” broker — the best one for you depends on what kind of coverage you need (ACA individual/family plan, small‑group for employees, short‑term, Medicare, etc.), how much personal hand‑holding you want, and whether you value in‑person service or are fine with remote support. I can find and compare highly rated local brokers if you tell me your ZIP code and what type of plan you want.

To help you pick a strong broker in Kansas City right away, here’s a practical approach and what to look for:

What to look for in a broker for self‑employed people
- Relevant experience: proven experience with ACA/individual marketplace plans and helping clients apply for premium tax credits and cost‑sharing reductions. If you have employees, look for experience with SHOP/small‑group plans.  
- Independent (non‑captive) vs captive: independent brokers represent multiple carriers and can shop around; captive agents only sell one company’s plans. For comparison shopping, prefer independent brokers.  
- Licensing and standing: confirm they’re licensed in Missouri (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup).  
- Transparency on fees/commissions: ask whether they charge a broker fee or are paid entirely by the insurer; a small broker fee is reasonable if you get extra help.  
- Client reviews & references: check Google, Yelp, Facebook and ask for references of self‑employed clients.  
- Ability to handle tax documentation: they should understand Form 1095‑A, advance premium tax credit reconciliation, and how subsidies are affected by income variation.  
- Availability and service model: do you want in‑person meetings in KC, phone/Zoom support, year‑round service (renewals, life changes, claims help)?  
- Knowledge of special programs: e.g., Medicaid, CHIP, COBRA, short‑term limitations, and local clinic networks in KC.

Where to search and verify brokers
- Healthcare.gov / Missouri marketplace (for ACA plans and subsidy eligibility).  
- HealthSherpa or eHealth (online enrollment platforms with broker support if you prefer mostly online).  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup (verify licensing and complaints).  
- Local referrals: Kansas City small‑business groups, SCORE, and local CPAs who work with self‑employed clients.

Questions to ask a broker before you commit
- Do you specialize in individual marketplace (ACA) plans for self‑employed people?  
- Are you independent? Which carriers do you work with?  
- Do you charge any broker fees? If so, how much and when?  
- Will you help with subsidy (advance premium tax credit) calculations and Form 1095‑A?  
- How will you support me at renewal time or if I have a claim problem?  
- Can I get references from other self‑employed clients?

If you want, I can:
- Search for 3–5 highly rated independent brokers in Kansas City with ACA experience and send you their names, contact info, and summary of reviews.  
- Or walk you through choosing a plan for your situation if you tell me estimated annual income, family size, ZIP code, and whether you want a low premium or low out‑of‑pocket costs.

Which would you prefer? (If you want specific broker names, give your ZIP code and whether you need individual/marketplace, small‑group, or Medicare help.)
